| [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) v3 | Individuality alone is not agency | Barandiaran, Di Paolo & Rohde (2009), [LIT-566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-566.md), read in [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md). The three conditions are that the system distinguishes itself from its environment with no observer doing it, that it is the active source of modulations of its coupling with the environment, and that it regulates that coupling against norms its own organisation sets. Each is necessary, and together they are claimed to be sufficient. Individuality is the precondition of the other two and does not suffice. A cell in passive osmosis, a kitten warmed by its mother and a person with a Parkinsonian tremor are each individuals, and none of them is acting. The generative definition is an open autonomous organisation that adaptively modulates its coupling so as to maintain itself. Here "autonomy" and "self" mean organisational closure. They do not mean a subject or self-governance. Proposed: a conceptual analysis checked against intuitive cases, with an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v5 | Organisms differ from flames by differentiation | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) v3 | Blanket placement is fixed by prior modelling | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. The formal core is [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): the partition takes the internal set as input. This account adds what the critiques show about practice. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the graph was built from one kind of coupling and steady state was assumed when the run stopped. In published applications the blanket sits wherever the model needs it: in the receptors of a brain, the membrane of a bacillus, the beam joining two pendulums. The formalism also gives the same description to a membrane the cell makes and a beam nobody's states make. So the blanket presupposes the boundary it is offered as the criterion of. Active since 2026-10-27, narrowed to the 2013 formulation and the applications held. The later steady-state definitions have not been read, and the unrestricted claim is THEORY-1097, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-135.md) v2 | Multicellularity is a cheater-suppression system | Aktipis et al. (2015), [LIT-740](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-740.md). Multicellularity requires cell-level fitness to be suppressed; cancer is cheating on five foundations of cellular cooperation. | [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) v2 | Transitions need between-collective selection | Okasha (2022), [LIT-749](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-749.md), restating with Buss and Michod a principle of the major transitions: a new collective can be undone by defectors, and succeeds only if higher-level selection trumps lower-level selection, usually through policing or aligned interests. The transitions make the hierarchy an explanandum. Proposed: a review stating general principles that Okasha himself says may explain any one transition only coarsely. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-217](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-217.md) | Malfunction needs no second-order norms | Barandiaran (2025), [LIT-1026](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1026.md), read in [NOTE-730](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-730.md). Against the dual-order account (Saborido, Moreno and Mossio), on which malfunction needs a regulated switch between regimes that a first-order trait fails to follow. The viability space has viable, precarious and terminal regions, and the normative field is the minimum constant parametric change at each precarious state that avoids disintegration. A trait functions when it correlates positively with the field, subfunctions when it does so too slowly, malfunctions when it does not, and is nonfunctional when it does nothing where it must. The standard is the organization's own viability, not a designer's goal, a selection history or a statistical norm. Proposed: a conceptual proposal with a one-variable model, and the field has not been computed for any real organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v5 | Self-maintenance grounds intrinsic function | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. A candle flame has functions in this sense. Representation arrives with recursive self-maintenance: a system that picks its next interaction by how it has differentiated its environment implicitly predicates that the interaction will succeed, and can find the predication false. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-221.md) v2 | Organizational closure differs from feedback | Rubin, Roli, Stano & Damiano (2026), [LIT-1027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1027.md), read in [NOTE-727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-727.md). A genealogy of closure notions from logic, cybernetics, systems theory, thermodynamics, relational biology and the biology of cognition, and an interpretive thesis drawn from it. The genealogy shows that "closure" names different things (information, operations, efficient causes, constraints, catalysts). The thesis picks efficient causes, adds that closure so read cannot be exhaustively described as a state-determined syntactic procedure, and concludes that current AI, agentic LLM systems included, is heteronomous. Proposed: the thesis is an interpretation, the irreducibility rests on Rosen's unassessed arguments and a halting-problem argument the authors call provisional, and the AI verdict is drawn from the definition, not from analysis of any system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md) v2 | Agency grows when parts resolve constraints | Watson (2023), [LIT-990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-990.md), read in full in [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md). A perspective essay's definition, argued and illustrated, not proved: agency of a whole with respect to its parts is the reduction in the parts' total frustration at equilibrium that its organization achieves over the old one, shown by directed uphill excursions to lower minima. It is comparative and sets no threshold for an additional agent, and it holds only relative to a stipulated decomposition and stipulated goals for the parts. That bottom-up learning produces such organization is reported from earlier models, not shown here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-413](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-413.md) | Units of selection need not be adapted | Lloyd's SEP entry (2005, revised 2024), [LIT-160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md), read in [NOTE-184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-184.md). | [THEORY-418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md) v4 | New individuality needs collaboration and closure | Griesemer & Shavit (2023), [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), read in [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md). | [THEORY-443](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-443.md) | Biological individuals needn't be organisms | Wilson and Barker (SEP, 2007; substantive revision 2024), [LIT-168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md), read in [NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md). | [THEORY-465](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-465.md) | Being reproduced does not entail reproducing | Bourrat (2025), [LIT-157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md), read in [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md). | [THEORY-473](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md) | Individual niche is mostly counterfactual | Takola & Schielzeth (2022), [LIT-127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-127.md), read in full in [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md). | [THEORY-492](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-492.md) | Geochemistry forced metabolism into existence | Morowitz & Smith (2006 working paper; Complexity 2007), [LIT-528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-528.md), read in [NOTE-425](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-425.md). | [THEORY-514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-514.md) | Constraint closure doesn't single out organisms | Baedke (2025), [LIT-167](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md), read in full in [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md). | [THEORY-532](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-532.md) | Life degrades applied gradients faster | Schneider & Kay (1994), [LIT-533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-533.md), read in [NOTE-415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-415.md). | [THEORY-607](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-607.md) v2 | Evolved individuals are coarse-grained summaries | Bourrat (2023), [LIT-049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md), read in full in [NOTE-064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-064.md). | [THEORY-612](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-612.md) | Niche construction can't cause selection itself | Hazelwood (2023), [LIT-156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md), read in full in [NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md). A dilemma against strong reciprocal causation in the extended evolutionary synthesis, aimed at Laland and colleagues. Its force rests on a process/product split for selection and a compositional reading of realization, both defended by citation and flagged as contestable, and its second horn considers only two non-emergent options. The weak sense, that organisms and environments affect each other, is granted as unobjectionable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md) v2 | Graded intrinsic norms need adaptivity | Di Paolo (2005), [LIT-1017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1017.md), read in full in [NOTE-719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md). A conceptual argument against Weber and Varela: autopoiesis in its original formulation entails conservation, not active homeostasis, so a bacterium whose intake is below consumption does not seek food "just because" it is autopoietic, and balancing at a cliff edge and falling over it both conserve autopoiesis. Adaptivity is defined, graded and recursive; pathology becomes failure of adaptivity while autopoiesis continues. There is no formal model, and the viability set is defined in one sentence. Proposed. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-666.md) | Autopoiesis gives organisms intrinsic purpose | Weber & Varela (2002), [LIT-1018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1018.md), read in full in [NOTE-720](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-720.md). | [THEORY-874](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-874.md) | Organicism is orthogonal to embodiment | Ward (2026), [LIT-1356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1356.md), read in the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-1065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1065.md). Views differ on where cognition's processes are (skull or brain–body–world) and, separately, on what the meaning of mental states depends on (information, or organization distinctive of the living). Embodied predictive processing, extended functionalism and cybernetics are embodied and informationalist; the enactive approach is organicist, and further marked by experiential primacy and reciprocity. The sharp edge: it is a taxonomy argued from examples and exegesis. It does not argue that organicism is true, and the line between distinctive and characteristic properties of life is left without a criterion. | Proposed |

That is a part that belongs to the system and not to "the responsible mechanism for that particular phenomenon". The clamp is an ideal intervention, cheap in a model and hard in vivo. It is not a test of where the system's boundary lies. | Active |
| [THEORY-1292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1292.md) | Drive removal tells self-sustained from damped | Bechtel and Abrahamsen (2010), [LIT-1936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1936.md), §3.6, p. 328, read in [NOTE-1492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1492.md). Peripheral clocks were once taken for "slaves" of the SCN, damping without it. Later evidence suggested they keep oscillating and lose synchrony, so the SCN is "a conductor" rather than "a ringmaster". The paper's reading is that models of both kinds "can reveal the empirical signatures that each may leave". This is a biological instance of the record's question where maintenance is realized. It is also a case outside [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s ideal limit: the outside drive does not reproduce the inside law, so a perturbation of state may tell them apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1351.md) v2 | Shared interests, not policing, drive transitions | West et al. (2015), [LIT-2003](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2003.md), read in [NOTE-1538](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1538.md). A colloquium review: the definition and the two steps are the authors' framework, and the explanatory claim is drawn from the comparative literature they cite. Proposed because they call it "tentative", and because the theory for transitions between species is missing on their own account. It differs from [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) on mechanism: group formation, not policing, does the work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1578](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1578.md) v2 | Parental care gives no evidence for altruism | A critique of Unto Others, read in full in [NOTE-1282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1282.md). Stich rejects the arguments from imperfect belief–affect correlation, from the cost of strong affect and from redundancy, and answers the argument from fragile beliefs. It leaves egoism open, not shown true. Filed from [NOTE-1282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1282.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1596](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1596.md) v2 | Grandparental diet tracks grandchild mortality | Pembrey, Saffery and Bygren (2014), a position paper of the Network in Epigenetic Epidemiology, read in place of Pembrey et al. 2006 ([NOTE-1320](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1320.md)). About 100 probands per cohort, one population, no measured family culture, and priors partly set after earlier results. It corrects [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s label: Överkalix is a male-line nutritional case, in which good supply, not poor, went with higher grandchild mortality, and the authors leave the mechanism open. | Active |
| [THEORY-1654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1654.md) | Microchimerism is bidirectional and long-lived | Chua and colleagues' consensus of 29 microchimerism researchers ([LIT-2415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2415.md), read in [NOTE-1768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1768.md)). The established half is what the owner's link to graded individuality needs as a premise; the open half is why it cannot yet carry more. Proposed because the established half rests on primary studies not read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1658.md) | LysM+CD11c+ maternal cells sustain tolerance | Peng, Way and colleagues' result as Cincinnati Children's reports it ([LIT-2428](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2428.md), read in [NOTE-1763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1763.md)). The persistence of foreign-origin cells in a host and their part in the host's regulation come apart: one marked subset does the tolerogenic work, and the rest persist without it. Proposed because the source is a press post and the paper could not be read; the Europe PMC abstract agrees with it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1675](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1675.md) | The foster is not shown to be part of the gravida | Geddes (2022), read in [NOTE-1732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1732.md) (Read). Kingma argued that the foster is part of the gravida, defending this against a "containment" view. Geddes shows that she treats rejection of parthood as acceptance of disjointness, so overlooking proper overlap (sharing some but not all parts). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1682.md) | The gut complex is constitutive of cognition | Boem, Greslehner, Konsman and Chiu, read in [NOTE-1765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1765.md) (Read). The authors argue that 4E (embodied, embedded, enactive, extended) accounts of cognition and perception have neglected the gut and should include the "gut complex": the enteric nervous, endocrine, mucosal immune and microbiota systems with gut tissue, a functional rather than anatomical unit interfacing with the lumen as an "internalized external environment". They defend two perspectives: (1) the gut complex plays an important role in the perception and cognition "of the subject as a whole"; (2) it has "its own forms of proto-cognition and perception". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1691.md) | Microchimeric cells form an extended immune self | Kinder, Stelzer, Arck and Way, read in [NOTE-1728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1728.md) (Read). A review arguing that the bidirectional transfer of cells between mother and fetus during pregnancy, and their persistence for decades (fetal cells in mothers: fetal microchimerism, FMC; maternal cells in offspring: maternal microchimerism, MMC), is not accidental but serves reproductive fitness: in mice, maternal microchimeric cells sustain offspring's regulatory T cell tolerance of non-inherited maternal antigens (NIMAs), which protects the offspring's own later pregnancies sired by NIMA-matched males (Kinder et al. 2015, ref. 14), and fetal cells retained in mothers may analogously protect later pregnancies (supported in humans by partner-specific protection against preeclampsia). Microchimeric cells may also replace injured tissue or be targets of alloimmunity resembling autoimmunity; causal roles in humans are mostly unestablished. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1704.md) | Fetal cells extend the placenta beyond the womb | Boddy, Fortunato, Wilson Sayres and Aktipis, read in [NOTE-1781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1781.md) (Read). An evolutionary (cooperation-and-conflict) framework for fetal microchimerism. Fetal cells cross into the mother, persist for decades, and have paradoxical associations with maternal health (both protective and harmful). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1711.md) | Kind onset and parthood in pregnancy separate | Finn, read in [NOTE-1753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1753.md) (Read). Finn separates two questions in the Kingma / Smith–Brogaard debate on the metaphysics of pregnancy. The **Timing Question**: when does an organism of the relevant kind start to exist (During-Pregnancy models such as Smith and Brogaard's sixteen days; After-Pregnancy models such as Kingma's "Nine Months")? | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2220.md) | A flame self-maintains without closure | Mossio and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2311](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2311.md) (Read). A flame is far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance through one constraint; an organism has organisational closure, a set of constraints each maintaining another that maintains it. Closure is partial, holds among constraints not processes, and is direct. It is necessary for an organism, not sufficient. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2221.md) | Regulation is second-order control | Bich, Mossio, Ruiz-Mirazo and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2310.md) (Read). Regulation is control exerted over the constitutive regime by a subsystem produced by it but dynamically decoupled from it, triggered by perturbations, that shifts the regime between viable states. Feedback depends on one constraint; closure is the mutual dependence of several. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md) | Sign content comes from producer–consumer history | Millikan (2009), "Biosemantics", [LIT-3103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3103.md), read in [NOTE-2324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2324.md) from her pre-print. Her own short statement of the selection-based teleosemantics the record said it owed ([LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md)). Teleology explains how a representation can be false; a mapping theory with producer and consumer explains what it represents. Corroborates [CLAIM-650](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md) on its question (a), with a qualification argued in [ARG-204](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-204.md); grounds the objection [CLAIM-920](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-920.md) to [CLAIM-648](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md). Proposed: one reading, of a compressed statement whose account of function is cited, not given. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2235](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2235.md) | Teleosemantics derives content from function | Neander and Schulte (2004; rev. 2022), SEP, "Teleological Theories of Mental Content", [LIT-3104](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3104.md), read in [NOTE-2325](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2325.md). A survey by two proponents, one of whom is surveyed. It reports the field's shape and its objections and settles little; the title asserts only what the survey reports. Read for [LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md) beside Millikan's own statement ([THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md)). Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2269.md) | Scaffolds can impose Darwinian properties first | Bourrat, Takacs, Doulcier, Nitschke, Black, Hammerschmidt and Rainey (2024), read in [NOTE-2362](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2362.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1940.md). A perspective piece: the two-peaks condition is borrowed from Doulcier et al. (2024) and the constructive route is proposed for future models. Its operative-cause definition assumes no feedback, which the constructive route is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2270.md) | Transitions complete when scaffolds internalize | Bourrat (2022), read in [NOTE-2361](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2361.md) (Read). The criterion (§2, Table 1) grades collective properties as pseudo-Darwinian, Darwinian-like and Darwinian by the source of the mechanisms producing them; the model (§5-6) lifts one part of the scaffold, the migration ban, and leaves patches, their capacity and the periodic propagule generations in place. The author calls the result preliminary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2271.md) | Neolithic was a transition in individuality | Shavit and Sharon (2023), read in [NOTE-2363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2363.md) (Read). An opinion paper: the stage assignments are made by fit with a published archaeological synthesis, and the authors say they do not examine how far the case meets ETI criteria. It is the application of [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md)'s sketch, not a test of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2273.md) | Entrenched elements resist evolutionary change | Wimsatt and Schank (2004), read in [NOTE-2365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2365.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1926](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1926.md). The definition is the paper's; the simulations mostly assign selection coefficients by class rather than compute entrenchment, so they bear on differential selection in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2275.md) | Reproducers develop and overlap with progeny | Wilkins and Bourrat's SEP entry (2022 revision), §5.4, read in [NOTE-2367](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2367.md) (Skimmed), a neighbour of [LIT-1932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1932.md) and [LIT-1937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1937.md). A survey's report of Griesemer, not Griesemer; one of its page citations points to the wrong paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2326.md) | Facial displays signal social motives, not emotions | Fridlund, *Human Facial Expression: An Evolutionary View* (1994). The account the record expects to draw from the work, attributed at the owner's direction of 2026-11-26 ("even deferred, you can still attribute to those works the theories we expect to draw from them"). It is stated from the assistant's prior knowledge of the work. The work is unread, so the statement is unverified until read, and it grounds nothing until then. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
